topics.name: Tesla Robotaxi Launch in Austin
topics.summary: Tesla launched a paid, driverless robotaxi service in Austin with a limited geofence and ~10 cars. Early riders praised its smoothness. The key thesis is Tesla's manufacturing scale (producing as many cars every 5 hours as Waymo's entire fleet) could let it dominate autonomous ride-hailing on cost per mile.

topics.name: The Social Network 2
topics.summary: Aaron Sorkin is returning as writer and director of a Social Network sequel. The hosts performed a satirical fake script featuring Zuckerberg and Nat Friedman debating the merits of open-sourcing Llama.

topics.name: Yacine / Dingboard
topics.summary: Yacine, a prolific tech poster and former X bug-fixing engineer, discussed leaving X after paternity leave complications, his meme-making app Dingboard, plans for robotics (a dandelion-picking lawn robot), and his custom NeoVim-based LLM coding setup.

topics.name: Iran Nuclear Facility Strike
topics.summary: The US struck Iran's Fordow nuclear facility using over a year's worth of GBU-57 Bunker Buster production. Iran retaliated against a US base in Qatar with no casualties. Polymarket still gave only 32% odds the facility was fully destroyed. Mike Gallagher framed it as a potentially historic setback for the Iran-Russia-China axis.

topics.name: Palantir and Nuclear Energy Partnership
topics.summary: Palantir's Mike Gallagher announced a partnership with The Nuclear Company to use Palantir software to accelerate nuclear reactor construction timelines, framed as essential for US AI energy competitiveness against China.

topics.name: GLP-1 Drug Market / Hims & Hers Novo Nordisk Breakup
topics.summary: Novo Nordisk terminated its partnership with Hims & Hers, accusing it of selling compounded knockoffs using Wegovy's brand. Hims stock dropped 32%. The ADA conference showcased advances including once-monthly injectables and muscle-preserving combo therapies. A gray-market guide writer claimed to have catalyzed nearly 12,000 pounds of weight loss.

topics.name: Shell Potential Acquisition of BP
topics.summary: The WSJ reported Shell is in early talks to acquire BP in what could be the largest oil deal since ExxonMobil's creation. Shell denied the report. BP has underperformed peers due to a failed renewables pivot and management issues.

topics.name: Fred Smith / FedEx Obituary
topics.summary: Tribute to FedEx founder Fred Smith, who died at 80. Highlighted his Yale hub-and-spoke thesis, Vietnam service, and building FedEx into a 500K-employee company with 700 aircraft and 200K vehicles from near-bankruptcy beginnings.

topics.name: Mr. Beast ViewStats AI Thumbnail Tool Rollback
topics.summary: Mr. Beast pulled his AI thumbnail generation tool from ViewStats after backlash from professional thumbnail artists, replacing it with a referral funnel to human artists. Hosts argued this was the wrong call given that millions of creators would benefit versus a few thousand thumbnail professionals.

topics.name: Neuralink Update
topics.summary: Neuralink reported 7 working human participants, including late-stage ALS patients. Demos included FPS gaming with dual joystick control. Roadmap includes speech decoding, Blindsight (vision restoration), inner-thought speed, and a future Neuralink app store. The surgical robot installs threads 1/20th the width of a human hair into the motor cortex.

topics.name: VC Marketing Strategy
topics.summary: Discussion of how venture capital firms should evolve their media strategy away from podcasts and X posts toward timeless formats like books, op-eds, and screenshot essays, citing Thiel, Naval, and Paul Graham as models. Also explored buying ads in prestige publications as a luxury brand-building play.

topics.name: NIH Funding Cuts
topics.summary: Cremu noted alarm at current NIH cuts but expressed optimism that deregulatory changes and new appointees would lead to increased and better-allocated biotech funding once the hiring freeze lifts.

topics.name: Congress Term Limits
topics.summary: Mike Gallagher discussed his bipartisan term limits bill (12 years each in House and Senate, grandfathering existing members) that briefly had White House support in 2017 but died due to leadership opposition. Argued structural incentives in Congress push members toward media over governance.

topics.name: AI Coding Tools
topics.summary: Yacine described his custom NeoVim-based LLM framework as a potential Cursor competitor, using Gemini 2.5 Pro as primary model for its cost, speed, and coding quality. Dismissed Cursor in favor of self-built tooling he can read and modify.
